  "title": "Demonstration-Grounded Warm-Start Hypothesis Elicitation for LLM Personalization via Binary Confirmation",
  "core_problem": "Personalizing LLMs to individual users requires efficient preference elicitation from few-shot demonstrations. Current methods exhibit three distinct failure modes: (1) Demonstration-grounded hypothesis methods (HyPerAlign) infer rich preference attributes from user examples but skip validation, risking hallucination and echo-chamber failure; (2) The BOED-for-preference-elicitation line—established by OPEN (arXiv 2403.05534, ACL 2024) and extended by BED-LLM (arXiv 2508.21184, ICLR 2026)—applies principled EIG-based adaptive questioning but initializes without user-specific demonstration-conditioned priors: OPEN uses LM-ranked feature importances as a domain-generic prior (not conditioned on any specific user's outputs); BED-LLM starts from an LM-generic prior p_f(θ;∅)—the LLM's own unconditional predictive distribution over hypotheses, not conditioned on any specific user's demonstrations—which is also not informed by available user examples; both waste elicitation turns on hypotheses that available user demonstrations already resolve; (3) Iterative preference inference from writing samples (PROSE, ICML 2025) refines free-form preference descriptions with component-level verification but involves no user interaction and no formal Bayesian posterior—it cannot adaptively resolve ambiguous hypotheses that demonstrations alone are insufficient to distinguish. Additionally, arXiv 2604.02485 ('Failing to Falsify', April 2026) shows LLMs exhibit systematic confirmation bias in hypothesis testing (42% baseline success rate), meaning LLM-generated hypothesis sets may be preferentially confirmable rather than genuinely falsifiable, causing Bayesian posteriors to converge spuriously on echo-chamber preference profiles. No existing method combines user-demonstration-conditioned warm-start Bayesian priors, EIG-based binary confirmation, and explicit disconfirmation-probe auditing in the LLM response-style personalization domain.",
  "opportunity": "The BOED-for-preference-elicitation lineage was established by OPEN (arXiv 2403.05534, ACL 2024), which combined EIG-based query selection with LM feature extraction over pairwise item comparisons in content recommendation—but initializes from LM-ranked feature importances (a domain-generic warm start reflecting general knowledge about what features matter for news article preferences, not this user's actual examples). BED-LLM (arXiv 2508.21184, ICLR 2026) extends OPEN to discrete language hypothesis sets with a Rao-Blackwellized EIG estimator and an LM-generic prior initialization p_f(θ;∅), evaluating on latent preference vector inference via movie-preference multiple-choice queries and 20-Questions, demonstrating that EIG-based sequential Bayesian elicitation substantially outperforms prompt-only baselines. Neither OPEN nor BED-LLM exploits K specific examples of a target user's actual outputs: their initializations duplicate information that demonstrations already encode, wasting early elicitation turns. AMPLe (arXiv 2411.00524, ACL 2025) addresses multi-dimensional LLM personalization via comparison-based active Bayesian elicitation, but also cold-starts from pairwise item comparisons rather than user demonstrations and lacks disconfirmation probes. HyPerAlign (arXiv 2505.00038, May 2025) showed demonstration-grounded hypotheses yield >90% win rates but explicitly omits user validation. PROSE (arXiv 2505.23815, ICML 2025) achieves 33% improvement over CIPHER on writing-style tasks via iterative preference refinement from demonstrations, but operates entirely without user interaction—it cannot distinguish two hypotheses with similar demonstration-level support, and provides no mechanism to surface or mitigate confirmation bias. The unaddressed gap is the warm-start interactive regime: when K demonstrations are available, initializing the Bayesian prior from user-specific demonstration-conditioned LLM likelihoods—calibrated via temperature scaling to avoid overconfident prior collapse—should dramatically reduce required elicitation turns compared to both OPEN and BED-LLM (testable claim), while the interactive EIG confirmation phase resolves the residual ambiguity that passive methods like PROSE cannot address (complementary claim). A second gap concerns confirmation bias: an elicitation system that does not deliberately seed disconfirmation probes in the hypothesis pool risks producing preference profiles that reflect what an LLM expects a user to prefer rather than what the user actually prefers—an echo-chamber failure mode that HyPerAlign acknowledges but does not address, and that PROSE's component-verification step partially mitigates without fully resolving.",
  "landscape": "The preference elicitation and personalization landscape includes eight relevant clusters. (1) Demonstration-grounded, no validation: HyPerAlign (arXiv 2505.00038, ICLR 2025 workshop) generates falsifiable-in-principle preference hypotheses from demonstrations and injects them as system prompts without user confirmation. (2) Iterative preference inference from writing samples, no interaction: PROSE (arXiv 2505.23815, ICML 2025, Aroca-Ouellette, Mackraz, Theobald, Metcalf; Apple ML Research) iteratively refines free-form preference descriptions from user writing samples via a generate→compare→update loop, then verifies preference components against held-out demonstrations with component-level scoring; achieves 33% improvement over CIPHER baseline on summarization and email writing tasks across Qwen2.5-7B/72B and GPT-4o variants; no user interaction beyond initial writing samples, no Bayesian posterior over hypotheses, no disconfirmation mechanism—the key differentiator from FABEL is that PROSE cannot adaptively resolve ambiguity beyond what demonstrations already encode and has no principled update when demonstrations are insufficient to distinguish competing hypotheses; must be included as a baseline (directly competitive with FABEL Stage 1) and explicitly differentiated. (3) The BOED-for-preference-elicitation lineage: OPEN (arXiv 2403.05534, ACL 2024, Handa, Gal, Pavlick, Goodman, Andreas, Tamkin, Li) established this line by combining EIG-based query selection with LM feature extraction for content recommendation—selects pairwise queries over binary feature vectors (|F|=10, e.g., 'discusses science') using a particle-filter Bayesian update with Bradley-Terry preference model; prior initialization is via LM-ranked feature importances (domain-generic: w_i = 1.2 − 0.12i for rank i), NOT conditioned on any specific user's demonstrations; evaluates NYT article recommendation (n=30 articles, ~40 Prolific users); outperforms LM-only and BOED-only baselines in user studies; no user-demonstration-conditioned warm start, no response-style personalization domain, no disconfirmation mechanism. BED-LLM (arXiv 2508.21184, ICLR 2026) extends OPEN to discrete language hypothesis sets: samples N=15 hypotheses per turn, selects questions via Rao-Blackwellized EIG estimator (~45–50 LLM calls/step), rejection-sampling Bayesian posterior update; starts from an LM-generic prior p_f(θ;∅)—the LLM's own unconditional distribution over hypotheses, not conditioned on any specific user's demonstrations (and notably over-collapsed toward a small number of hypothesis types per the paper); uses multiple-choice questions (a technical requirement: having a small space of single-token responses ensures p_LLM provides meaningful uncertainty over outcomes for EIG estimation); evaluates on latent preference vector inference via movie-preference multiple-choice queries and the 20-Questions game; no public code. Active Task Disambiguation (arXiv 2502.04485, ICLR 2025) similarly applies Bayesian experimental design for clarifying question selection on under-specified tasks. FABEL extends beyond all three works: (i) user-specific demonstration-conditioned warm start (K=5–10 demos from THIS user, vs. OPEN's domain-generic LM-ranked feature importances and BED-LLM's demo-agnostic LM-generic prior p_f(θ;∅)), (ii) temperature-scaled prior calibration to prevent overconfident prior collapse, (iii) binary yes/no natural-language hypothesis confirmation over free-form response-style attributes (vs. OPEN's pairwise item comparisons and BED-LLM's multiple-choice format—FABEL's binary format reduces cognitive load while remaining viable because hypothesis confirmation questions are naturally binary in ways that preference inference over open hypothesis spaces is not), (iv) mandatory disconfirmation probes in the EIG pool (absent from all prior BOED-for-preference work), (v) application to LLM response-style personalization (format, tone, structure)—a domain shift from BED-LLM's latent preference vector inference. (3b) Comparison-based active preference learning for LLM personalization: AMPLe (arXiv 2411.00524, ACL 2025, Oh, Lee, Ok; POSTECH; public code: github.com/ml-postech/AMPLe) personalizes LLM outputs to implicit multi-dimensional preferences via pairwise comparison queries, a modified Bayesian posterior update robust to noisy feedback, and generalized binary-search-inspired active query selection. AMPLe is directly adjacent to FABEL in the active Bayesian personalization space but differs in three critical ways: (1) AMPLe cold-starts from pairwise item comparisons rather than initializing from user demonstrations; (2) AMPLe asks 'which response do you prefer?' (item comparison) rather than 'does this stylistic hypothesis apply to you?' (hypothesis confirmation); (3) AMPLe includes no disconfirmation probe mechanism. AMPLe must be cited as an ACL 2025 active Bayesian personalization baseline; its comparison-based query design and FABEL's hypothesis-confirmation design represent complementary elicitation paradigms. (4) Generative open-ended elicitation: GATE (arXiv 2310.11589, ICLR 2025, Li, Tamkin, Goodman, Andreas) uses free-form LLM-generated questions in three domains; its binary yes/no variant reduces cognitive load but underperforms the open-ended variant because binary questions without a Bayesian posterior cannot adaptively narrow the hypothesis space—GATE's binary variant also does not ground questions in user demonstrations. (5) Trajectory-optimized clarification: TO-GATE (arXiv 2506.02827) applies DPO to clarifying question quality, remaining in the open-ended, non-Bayesian regime. (6) Bayesian-RL hybrid: PEBOL (arXiv 2405.00981, RecSys 2024) combines NLI-based preference beliefs with Thompson Sampling in recommendation. (7) Bayesian in-context conditioning from demonstrations (adjacent): Variational In-Context Reward Modeling / ICRM (arXiv 2602.08819, Feb 2026, Hong, Tang, Wang) casts reward modeling as amortized variational inference over a latent preference with a conjugate Beta prior conditioned on in-context preference demonstrations at test time without retraining—conceptually adjacent to FABEL's warm-start initialization from demonstrations but differs in three critical ways: domain (pairwise scalar reward modeling vs. interactive response-style personalization), hypothesis representation (continuous Beta prior on scalar rewards vs. discrete binary preference hypotheses), and interaction mode (passive in-context update vs. active EIG confirmation loop); no disconfirmation probes; acknowledged in related work to pre-empt warm-start novelty challenge. (8) Few-shot preference optimization: FSPO (arXiv 2502.19312, 2025) meta-learns personalization from few-shot preference data; deferred to Phase 2 due to meta-training infrastructure overhead. The specific combination absent from all prior work: user-specific demonstration-conditioned Bayesian prior initialization + temperature-scaled calibration + EIG-based binary yes/no confirmation + mandatory disconfirmation probes + application to LLM response-style personalization (format, tone, structure)—distinct from AMPLe's comparison-based cold-start design, OPEN's domain-generic warm start, BED-LLM's demo-agnostic LM-generic prior with multiple-choice format, and PROSE's non-interactive refinement.",
  "approach": "We propose FABEL (Falsification-Aligned Binary Elicitation Loop), a tuning-free framework operating in four stages. The EMNLP 2026 submission is scoped as an MVP: PersonalLLM benchmark, four baselines, one LLM backbone (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct), one core ablation, and a small crowdsourced human evaluation (n≈20) to strengthen the EMNLP Main case.

Stage 1—Demonstration-Grounded Hypothesis Generation with Disconfirmation Probes: Given K=5–10 few-shot user output demonstrations, a frontier open-source LLM (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) generates N_pos=12–15 falsifiable, binary-verifiable preference hypotheses (e.g., 'User prefers bulleted structure over prose') AND K_neg=4–6 explicit disconfirmation probes—hypotheses deliberately constructed to be easily falsifiable given the demonstrations (e.g., 'User avoids technical terminology' when demonstrations frequently use it). This two-class design, motivated by arXiv 2604.02485's finding that LLMs default to generating confirmable hypotheses, ensures the EIG pool contains falsifying evidence.

Stage 2—Temperature-Scaled Warm Prior Initialization with Calibration Check: Each hypothesis posterior is initialized as p(h_i = true | demos) ∝ exp(score_i / τ), where score_i is the LLM log-likelihood of the K demonstrations given hypothesis h_i, and τ is a temperature hyperparameter controlling prior sharpness. Raw LLM log-likelihoods are typically overconfident (τ=1); τ is selected on a held-out 50-user PersonalLLM dev split as the smallest value such that the prior Spearman rank correlation with ground-truth held-out-demo accuracy exceeds 0.6 (validation threshold). τ→∞ recovers a uniform prior (a maximally uninformative cold start, distinct from BED-LLM's LM-generic prior p_f(θ;∅), which reflects the LLM's own unconditional distribution over hypotheses and is neither uniform nor user-specific); τ=1 applies raw likelihoods. This design directly addresses LLM miscalibration: it ensures the warm start concentrates mass on demonstration-consistent hypotheses while avoiding premature posterior collapse onto incorrect hypotheses. The calibration analysis—Stage 2a in the paper—reports Spearman ρ between LLM log-likelihoods and empirical hypothesis accuracy across 50 PersonalLLM dev users, validating the warm-start assumption empirically and providing a lightweight check that does not require additional model training. Empirical hypothesis accuracy is operationalized as follows: for each simulated PersonalLLM dev user u (a weighted ensemble of 10 reward models with Dirichlet-sampled weights) and each hypothesis h_i, empirical accuracy = fraction of u's top-quartile responses (by u's weighted-ensemble reward score across the 8 candidate responses per prompt) that satisfy h_i, as assessed by prompting Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct to classify each response as satisfying or violating h_i. Spearman ρ is then computed between the vector of LLM log-likelihood scores [score_1, …, score_N] and the vector of empirical accuracies [acc_1, …, acc_N] across all N hypotheses, averaged over the 50 dev users. This operationalization is fully automated using PersonalLLM's existing reward-model infrastructure without additional human labels.

Stage 3—EIG-Based Binary Elicitation Loop with Disconfirmation Quota (algorithm specification): The full hypothesis set H = H_pos ∪ H_neg is placed in a single EIG-ranked pool. At each turn, FABEL selects the hypothesis with maximum posterior entropy H(p(h_i)) — nearest to log 2 — and poses it as a binary yes/no confirmation. The posterior updates via Bayes' rule with a noise term calibrated on held-out demo pairs. We apply a factored (independent) posterior approximation, updating each hypothesis probability independently; under this approximation, marginal entropy maximization H(p(h_i)) is equivalent to EIG-based selection. The loop terminates when joint preference entropy drops below threshold θ (empirically 3–5 turns).

Disconfirmation probe handling follows option (a)—probes are included in the EIG pool and selected by EIG only when maximally uncertain. This is algorithmically cleanest: EIG without H_neg would face a pool containing only confirmatory hypotheses, creating a structural selection bias toward echo-chamber convergence regardless of EIG's own informativeness criterion. Including H_neg in the pool makes the probe design a prior-shaping device rather than a scheduling override—EIG's entropy criterion then serves as a bidirectional diagnostic. If H_neg probes are never selected (prior already confidently classifies them as false), this is evidence of good prior calibration; if frequently selected (probes have high posterior entropy at elicitation start), this signals prior miscalibration requiring attention.

Soft minimum quota: To prevent the degenerate case where warm-start prior overconfidence silently suppresses all falsifying questions, at least ⌈K_neg / 3⌉ disconfirmation probes must be asked if the loop runs ≥3 turns. Quota-forced questions bypass EIG ordering for their designated turn but receive normal Bayesian updates. The 'disconfirmation selection rate'—fraction of turns where EIG (prior to quota enforcement) would have selected a H_neg hypothesis—is reported as a diagnostic distinguishing well-calibrated priors (low rate: probes already resolved by warm start) from miscalibrated ones (high rate: probes still maximally uncertain at elicitation start). The falsification rate—fraction of posterior updates that decrease hypothesis probability—is reported as a secondary diagnostic.

Stage 4—Personalized Generation: The confirmed/disconfirmed hypothesis set is injected as a structured system prompt without fine-tuning.

MVP Experimental Design (EMNLP 2026 ARR deadline May 25, 2026):
- Benchmark: PersonalLLM (ICLR 2025), using its reward-model-based simulated user evaluation infrastructure (public dataset: HuggingFace namkoong-lab/PersonalLLM); simulated evaluation eliminates GPT-4-judge latency and cost, enabling full experimental sweep within the 15-day window
- Human evaluation study (EMNLP Main strengthening, optional stretch): n≈20 crowdsourced participants via Prolific; each participant interacts with FABEL over 10 PersonalLLM prompts and evaluates personalized vs. baseline responses; setup requires ~1 agent-day (days 3–4, running in parallel with automated experiments); cost ~$100–200; even underpowered for significance, a real-user study demonstrates applicability beyond simulated personas and substantially strengthens the EMNLP Main case per reviewer guidance
- Backbone: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (single backbone for all methods)
- Baselines (4): (1) HyPerAlign—demonstration-grounded, no validation; (2) GATE binary—binary questions, no Bayesian posterior, no demonstration grounding; (3) PROSE—iterative preference inference from demonstrations, no user interaction, no Bayesian posterior; applied by running PROSE's generate→compare→update pipeline on PersonalLLM demonstrations, evaluating via reward model; (4) BED-LLM—LM-generic-prior EIG Bayesian with multiple-choice questions; reimplemented from paper description (no public code; Rao-Blackwellized EIG estimator + rejection-sampling update, ~45–50 LLM calls/step); time-boxed to 3–4 agent-days with fallback to 'BED-LLM-approx' (entropy-based selection + rejection-sampling, no full RB-EIG) if faithful replication is infeasible, with explicit labeling
- Core ablation (1): warm-start prior (τ-scaled from demos) vs. uniform prior (τ→∞), directly isolating the demonstration-grounded initialization contribution
- Primary metrics: PersonalLLM reward-model win rates (main); average elicitation turns (efficiency); disconfirmation selection rate + falsification rate (diagnostics); human preference rates if study included
- Phase 2 extensions (camera-ready / full paper): LaMP-4/6/7 text generation benchmarks; AMPLe and FSPO baselines; full ablation battery (probes included vs. excluded; EIG vs. random ordering; K sensitivity N∈{3,5,10}; τ sensitivity; full BED-LLM replication verification); additional backbone (Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct or Llama 4 Maverick)",

  "description": "Personalizing LLMs to individual users is hindered by three complementary failure modes: HyPerAlign generates demonstration-grounded preference hypotheses but skips user validation; the BOED-for-preference-elicitation line—established by OPEN (ACL 2024) and extended by BED-LLM (ICLR 2026)—applies principled EIG-based Bayesian elicitation but lacks user-specific demonstration-conditioned priors (OPEN uses domain-generic LM-ranked feature importances; BED-LLM uses an LM-generic prior p_f(θ;∅)—the LLM's own unconditional predictive distribution, not conditioned on any specific user's demonstrations); and PROSE (ICML 2025) iteratively refines free-form preference descriptions from writing samples but has no user interaction and no formal Bayesian posterior, leaving ambiguous hypotheses unresolved. AMPLe (ACL 2025) addresses multi-dimensional LLM personalization via comparison-based active Bayesian elicitation but also cold-starts from pairwise comparisons and lacks disconfirmation probes. We propose FABEL (Falsification-Aligned Binary Elicitation Loop), which extends the OPEN→BED-LLM BOED lineage by (1) initializing a temperature-scaled warm Bayesian prior p(h_i) ∝ exp(score_i / τ) from K=5–10 user-specific demonstrations—user-specific rather than domain-generic or demo-agnostic; (2) including K_neg=4–6 explicit disconfirmation probes in the EIG-ranked hypothesis pool, making the probe design a prior-shaping device that ensures EIG always has access to falsifying evidence; (3) applying a soft minimum quota (⌈K_neg/3⌉ probes if ≥3 turns) to prevent warm-start overconfidence from silently suppressing falsifying questions; (4) applying a factored posterior approximation with EIG-based binary yes/no confirmation (vs. BED-LLM's multiple-choice format, which is required for reliable LLM uncertainty quantification but increases cognitive load) to resolve remaining uncertainty in 3–5 turns; and (5) explicitly acknowledging that under the factored (independent) posterior approximation, marginal entropy maximization is equivalent to EIG-based selection. ## Key Findings:

**LLM-Prior Framework (Most Recent - August 2025)**

The LLMPrior framework automates and scales the elicitation and aggregation of prior distributions using Large Language Models. It introduces a principled operator that translates unstructured context into a valid, tractable PDF by architecturally coupling an LLM with an explicit generative model. The framework successfully demonstrated capability to elicit both simple conjugate priors (Beta distributions) and more complex, multi-modal priors (Gaussian Mixture Models).

**Bayesian Optimization with LLM-Based Acquisition Functions (2024)**

Preference elicitation methodologies that can quickly determine user's top item preferences in cold-start settings is key for personalized conversational recommendation systems. While LLMs enable natural language PE dialogues, they lack the multi-turn, decision-theoretic reasoning required to balance exploration and exploitation of user preferences. The PEBOL algorithm uses Natural Language Inference between user preference utterances and NL item descriptions to maintain Bayesian preference beliefs, and BO strategies such as Thompson Sampling and Upper Confidence Bound to steer LLM query generation.

**Cold-Start Personalization with Structured World Models (February 2026)**

Research evaluates approaches on four reasoning domains: medical (MedQA), mathematical (AIME), commonsense (CSQA), and social (SocialIQA). This addresses cold-start preference elicitation by decomposing the problem into offline learning of preference structure and online Bayesian experimental design.

**Bayesian Elicitation with LLMs (April 2026)**

Larger, more capable models produce more accurate estimates, but increasing reasoning effort provides no consistent benefit. All models are severely overconfident with their 95% intervals containing the true value only 9–44% of the time.

These papers collectively address the intersection of LLM capabilities with Bayesian personalization and preference elicitation methods.

## Paper Overview

The paper is titled "Many Preferences, Few Policies: Towards Scalable Language Model Personalization", and it was submitted on April 5, 2026.

## Problem and Solution

The paper addresses the challenge that while the ideal scenario for LLM personalization is a single LLM for each user perfectly aligned with their preferences, maintaining a separate LLM per user is impractical due to constraints on compute, memory, and system complexity.

The researchers developed a principled method for selecting a small portfolio of LLMs that captures representative behaviors across heterogeneous users, modeling user preferences across multiple traits (e.g., safety, humor, brevity) through a multi-dimensional weight vector.

## Key Innovation

Their algorithm PALM (Portfolio of Aligned LLMs) generates a small portfolio of LLMs such that, for any weight vector, the portfolio contains a near-optimal LLM for the corresponding scalarized objective. This is the first result that provides theoretical guarantees on both the size and approximation quality of LLM portfolios for personalization.

## Authors

The authors are Cheol Woo Kum, Jai Moondra, Roozbeh Nahavandi, Andrew Perrault, Milind Tambe, and Swati Gupta.
